question: Do candidates/approach_a or candidates/approach_b beat the shipped agent's 0.916125, judged under the repo's own rules (official score is reported, artifacts are not gains, adversarial axes are the private-set risk)?

protocol.splits: dev/holdout computed by sample_id against analysis/dev.jsonl within the single 200-session run; the agent's online elicitation adaptation therefore carries from dev into holdout, which is why baseline holdout reads 0.90885 here against the recorded fresh-agent 0.90555
protocol.adversarial: tools.adversarial.Adversarial and drifted_categories, seed 0, mirroring tools/bench.run_adversarial; baseline comparison rows are the recorded values in SKILL.md / analysis/v4_end_to_end_controls.json
protocol.baseline_reproduction: src.agent.Agent reproduced 0.916125 exactly (HR 1.000, MRR 0.773417, MTTC 1.795) before either candidate was measured

approach_a.name: recency- and correction-aware evidence (width-1 probe commit)

commit_artifact_control.what: Approach A's own env knobs forced to fixed width 10 (P_PROBE=10 P_UNSURE=10 P_WIDEN=1), removing the base_width=1 probe that makes every hit rank 1 by construction
commit_artifact_control.reading: At equal width its retrieval is worse than the shipped agent's recorded 0.90073 / MRR 0.710. The entire +0.018 official gain, and more, is the commit-width simulator artifact the shadow evaluator exists to remove.

expected_private_under_v4_prior.prior: 0.50 clean, 0.20 natural, 0.15 granularity, 0.10 one heavy axis, 0.05 multi-axis (V4_SCORE_AND_HEADROOM_ANALYSIS.txt section 2.2)

approach_a.why: The official gain is bought entirely by the width-1 probe commit, a documented simulator artifact; the mechanism it claims to contribute (evidence recency/epochs) sits on retrieval that is 0.026 weaker than shipped at equal width, breaks HR@10 1.000 on the clean public set, and collapses on every axis the private set is likely to move: -0.155 on category, -0.175 on granularity=1, -0.254 on granularity=3. Its routing is unstemmed token overlap with no semantic route, which is what the granularity rows are measuring.
approach_a.kept: Nothing. The correction-epoch idea is already shipped in src as question epochs and explicit restarts (V3), measured there at official parity.

approach_b.name: structured-evidence reranking (field BM25 + coverage + soft facets)

as_shipped.why: Written against an older src.routing interface: its Catalog lacks bucket_stems and bucket_by_key, so src.routing.candidates raises AttributeError on every turn and the agent's own except clause converts every response to zero recommendations. The candidate had never successfully executed a single turn before this benchmark.

shim.what: bucket_by_key and bucket_stems added to approach_b's Catalog instance post-construction, computed exactly as src/catalog.py lines 119-154 compute them (normalise(name), sorted-token alias, stemmed bucket tokens, max_bucket_words). Nothing else changed.

approach_b.why: As shipped it scores zero; interface-repaired it is -0.029 under control (MRR 0.670 vs 0.773), worse on both splits, and -0.135 on the category axis. Its findings.json-derived question prior never becomes load-bearing because the ranking underneath it loses before elicitation matters. The +0.015 scaffold reading is a single unpaired point inside the noise band.

conclusion: Neither candidate ships. The shipped agent remains 0.916125. Approach A is a live demonstration of the commit-width artifact: +0.018 official, worse retrieval, and an expected private-set cost of roughly -0.04 under the recorded paraphrase prior.
